All stages - procurement plans, public calls, tender documentation, decisions, complaints, contracts and execution reports - must pass through it, so banking/payments-adjacent lots (POS terminals, card personalisation, payment gateways, cash handling, self-service kiosks, core banking/treasury software) surface here first and in full technical detail.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: Unconstrained local-language queries waste budget and risk ingesting foreign-jurisdiction notices into a Montenegro dataset.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegrin-language equivalents were found for CPV-style commodity vocabulary specific to payments hardware (e.g. an official local term list for 'card personalisation', 'payment gateway', 'self-service kiosk').
negative_findings.result_summary: Local vocabulary confirmed only for: POS terminal(i), platni promet, elektronska fiskalizacija, fiskalna kasa, eFaktura, elektronski sertifikat, bankarski softver. English-in-local terms (POS, gateway, kiosk) are likely used verbatim in specifications.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Keyword filters must include untranslated English terms inside Montenegrin documents, or payments lots will be missed.

negative_findings.description: The appeals commission does NOT sit on the assumed kzp.gov.me domain; its decisions are published at kontrola-nabavki.me (contact komisija@nabavka.gov.me, Novaka Miloševa 28, Podgorica).
negative_findings.result_summary: Assumed domain wrong; correct domain identified and recorded as a candidate.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents a false 'dead source' record and locates a high-value decision archive.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Serbian for a standalone 'registar zaključenih ugovora' (register of concluded contracts) for Montenegro, as a separate artefact from CEJN. No distinct national contract register with its own URL was found.
negative_findings.result_summary: All evidence points to concluded contracts being published as a module inside CEJN rather than as a separately branded register. No independent registar-ugovora domain surfaced across four sr-language queries.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The collector must not wait for a 'contract register' endpoint that does not exist; the contract layer has to be extracted from CEJN (or its nabavke.com mirror) and from per-authority pages.

negative_findings.description: Targeted sr/en searches combining award vocabulary with banking-and-payments vocabulary ('bankarska oprema', 'platne kartice', 'payment services supplier value') returned no Montenegrin award decision or contract in the banking/payments domain.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches surfaced the correct document types (Odluka o izboru najpovoljnije ponude PDFs) but only for unrelated subjects — printing services, event equipment, transport tickets. No banking-equipment or card-services award was retrievable through general web search.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: It indicates that sector-relevant awards are not reachable by public search-engine indexing and must be reached by querying CEJN/nabavke.com by CPV code or authority, not by keyword. This shapes the collection design fundamentally.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Serbian for 'plan javnih nabavki 2026 Crna Gora'. Almost all results were Serbian (RS) authorities' 2026 plans, not Montenegrin ones.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only one Montenegrin plan page surfaced (Skupština Crne Gore), and that returned HTTP 403. Montenegrin 2026 annual plans appear to be published inside CEJN rather than as separately indexed web pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The January pipeline signal — the main forward-looking value of this cell — is not harvestable by search engine. It requires direct enumeration inside CEJN and site-by-site probing of authority '/javne-nabavke/plan-javne-nabavke' paths.

negative_findings.description: Serbian-language queries about Montenegro consistently returned Serbian (RS) results because both countries use identical procurement terminology and Serbia's jnportal.ujn.gov.rs / ujn.gov.rs domains outrank Montenegro's ujn.gov.me.
negative_findings.result_summary: Multiple queries returned mpravde.gov.rs, jnportal.ujn.gov.rs, mgsi.gov.rs and ejn.gov.ba instead of ME sources; Bosnian (ejn.gov.ba) contamination also occurred.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any automated sr-language query layer for Montenegro must pin the domain (site:.me, gov.me, cejn.gov.me, nabavke.com) or add 'Crna Gora'/'crnogorski' disambiguators, or the corpus will silently fill with Serbian and Bosnian records.

negative_findings.description: Direct fetches of both cejn.gov.me and nabavke.com returned only a bare heading ('CeJN', 'Portal javnih nabavki') with no navigation, links or document lists.
negative_findings.result_summary: Both are client-rendered single-page applications. This is a HYPOTHESIS of JS-gating, not a liveness verdict — both are clearly live, since nabavke.com serves indexed PDFs and detail pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Static HTTP collection will yield nothing from the two most important sources. Budget for a headless browser or, preferably, reverse-engineer the XHR/JSON endpoints behind the search views.

negative_findings.description: No register, obligation or aggregated source was found that publishes vendor selections or signed contracts of Montenegro's commercial banks (CKB, NLB, Hipotekarna, Erste, Lovćen, Prva banka, Universal Capital Bank).
negative_findings.result_summary: Private banks are outside Zakon o javnim nabavkama. The only outcome traces found were bank saopštenja and trade press, both incidental and non-systematic.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For sector=both, roughly half the addressable market has no outcome-side register at all. Award-tracking coverage for private banking is structurally unavailable and must be substituted with press, bank notices and supplier reference lists.

negative_findings.description: skupstina.me returned HTTP 403 Forbidden on a plain fetch of its procurement-plan page.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded as bot-defended-but-live (hypothesis), not as dead. Not retried with alternative headers in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Per-authority plan pages will need browser-grade fetching; a naive HTTP collector would wrongly mark many Montenegrin authority pages as unavailable.

negative_findings.description: No openly published 'lista ovlašćenih proizvođača fiskalnih uređaja' / approved fiscalisation-software-producer list was located for Montenegro, despite targeted local-language searching. Sources confirm a registration procedure for software producers exists (with the tax authority publishing instructions and a contact address efiskalizacija@tax.gov.me) but no public roster surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two sr-language searches returned only vendor marketing pages and employer-association explainers; no official vendor list.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This was the single highest-value pointer in the cell rationale — it would map the entire POS/terminal supply chain in one document. Its absence means the supply-chain map must be reconstructed indirectly from vendor self-declaration plus procurement award notices.

negative_findings.description: AZZK published a notice (dated Jan 2026) that access to the register of granted state aid and the de-minimis register requires a submitted access request, indicating the registers are not openly browsable even though annual aggregate reports are public.
negative_findings.result_summary: Register likely gated; annual state-aid reports (e.g. EUR 2.87m granted in 2025) remain public via AZZK and press.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Beneficiary-level state-aid data would complement award notices; if gated, we fall back to annual report PDFs at lower granularity.

negative_findings.description: No searchable member directory (imenik članova) was found for the Chamber of Economy of Montenegro; searches surfaced only governance pages, contacts and social media.
negative_findings.result_summary: komora.me appears to lack an open member-search facility.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Chamber directories are usually a cheap vendor-enumeration shortcut; here the ICT vendor population must instead be derived from CRPS activity codes and procurement bidder lists.

negative_findings.description: The CRPS public search and several CRPS content pages are served over plain HTTP (http://www.pretraga.crps.me/, http://crps.me/strana/pregled/NN) with an id-based URL scheme, alongside a parallel tax-administration portal (efirma.tax.gov.me). Which of the three is the canonical, maintained front end is unclear.
negative_findings.result_summary: Three overlapping CRPS front ends observed; none confirmed canonical.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A collection pipeline built on the wrong host risks silent breakage; the numeric /strana/pregled/NN paths are also likely to shift.

negative_findings.description: The tax authority's fiscalisation programme URL was inferred from the official contact address domain (tax.gov.me) rather than from a search-result link; the institution has also been renamed/merged into 'Uprava prihoda i carina', so content may now sit under gov.me.
negative_findings.result_summary: No direct search hit on an official efiskalizacija landing page.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The authoritative fiscalisation vendor and specification documents are the cell's key asset; the entry point must be pinned down before monitoring is set up.

negative_findings.description: English-language searching for Montenegrin registers returns mostly commercial aggregators and wikipedia rather than the registers themselves; substantive discovery in this cell was only possible in Serbian/Montenegrin.
negative_findings.result_summary: English queries produced low-value results; sr queries produced all authoritative hits.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms local-language collection is mandatory for ME A2, and that any monitoring keyword set must be built from sr terms (registar, spisak, pretraga, ponuđač, naručilac, javne nabavke).

negative_findings.description: Opentender.eu / DIGIWHIST, the main EU-funded procurement transparency scraper, does not list Montenegro among its ~33-35 covered jurisdictions (Serbia and North Macedonia are covered; Montenegro is not).
negative_findings.result_summary: No ME dataset found on opentender.eu; only regional comparators exist.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: There is no free, standardised, red-flag-enriched ME procurement dataset from the EU research ecosystem. Any structured ME analysis must rely on the national portal, opendata.gov.me, or paid aggregators — which raises both cost and access-review burden for this workstream.

negative_findings.description: No public GitHub scraper or open-source ingestion project dedicated to Montenegro's cejn.gov.me / CeJN e-procurement system was found.
negative_findings.result_summary: Generic tender-scraper repos (CivicDataLab/tender-scrapers-be, dobtco/openrfps-scrapers, okfde/opentender.eu) exist, but none target ME.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms a build-vs-buy decision: automated ME notice collection would need to be written from scratch, making the commercial aggregators (eKapija, eTenderi.me, TenderiLIVE) more attractive despite paywalls.

negative_findings.description: eTenderi.me could not be fetched — the fetch attempt returned a connection error rather than an HTTP status.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search-engine snippets describe the service in detail (SMS/e-mail/push alerts, competitor win rates, State Commission decisions database), so the site is presumed live but unfetched.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This is potentially the single most valuable ME-specific commercial source in this cell; its liveness and paywall terms must be confirmed by the deterministic verification pass before any access decision.

negative_findings.description: No aggregator was found that offers a banking/payments-specific bid-alert vertical for Montenegro or the Western Balkans.
negative_findings.result_summary: All identified aggregators are horizontal (all CPV sectors) and require keyword/CPV filtering by the subscriber; searches in both sr and en produced no banking-only or fintech-only tender service for ME.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sector focus must be engineered on our side via CPV codes and a sr/en keyword lexicon (bankarska oprema, bankomati, POS terminali, kartično poslovanje, core banking); no vendor does it for us.

negative_findings.description: No established Montenegrin/Serbian-language term was found for 'bid-alert service' or 'tender aggregator' as a product category.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local market instead uses descriptive phrasing ('portal javnih nabavki', 'obavještenja o tenderima', 'dnevni bilten', 'pronađi tendere') and English-in-local brand names (TenderiLIVE, eTenderi). 'Tenderi' alone is a very noisy term.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Local-language discovery must go through descriptive service phrases and brand names rather than a category noun, otherwise recall for this cell is systematically low.

negative_findings.description: Both https://www.dri.co.me/revizorski-izvjestaji and https://dri.co.me/revizorski-izvjestaji failed with 'unable to verify the first certificate' on WebFetch.
negative_findings.result_summary: Could not enumerate the DRI audit-report archive structure directly. Search-engine evidence shows many live PDFs under dri.co.me/doc/ and live /aktuelnost/ pages, so the site is almost certainly up — this is a TLS-chain/fetch-client issue, NOT a dead source.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: DRI is the single most important source in this cell; the collection pipeline must be configured with a full CA bundle (or an intermediate-fetching client) or it will silently drop the highest-value source.

negative_findings.description: MANS 'Javne nabavke' category index (https://www.mans.co.me/kategorija/javne-nabavke/) fetched successfully but rendered essentially one 2009 explainer article with no listed sub-items, reports or datasets.
negative_findings.result_summary: No downloadable MANS procurement dataset or report list was found at the obvious category URL in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: MANS's procurement material is likely behind tag pages, site search, or a separate publications/database section; a naive category crawl would wrongly conclude MANS publishes almost nothing on procurement.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated auditor/watchdog source was found that specifically covers procurement of BANKING or PAYMENT-sector IT (core banking, card/POS, payment infrastructure) in Montenegro.
negative_findings.result_summary: DRI IT audits located in this pass cover health (IZIS, health insurance fund, PCR app), sport registry and cultural-heritage systems. Watchdog procurement work (IA, MANS) is sector-agnostic or defence/security-focused.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For the banking/payments run scope, oversight coverage must be reached indirectly — via auditees that are financial in nature (Uprava prihoda i carina, Fond zdravstvenog osiguranja, Ministarstvo finansija, Centralna banka) rather than by topic search.

negative_findings.description: The session's web-search budget (200/200) was exhausted before I could run planned queries on the parliamentary oversight track (Odbor za ekonomiju, finansije i budžet consideration of DRI reports) and on the procurement inspectorate's published findings.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two intended snowball branches were not executed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The parliamentary committee track is where DRI findings become political follow-up and where non-published contracts sometimes get named; it remains an unexplored pointer branch for this cell.

negative_findings.description: mojnovac.me and mojgrad.me URLs were inferred from portal names reported in Montenegrin media coverage rather than fetched directly.
negative_findings.result_summary: Portals are well documented as existing and IA-operated, but the exact live URLs and whether they expose machine-readable endpoints was not established in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These are the only structured NGO-built spending datasets identified in the cell; their machine-readability determines whether they are a data source or just a browsing tool.

negative_findings.description: The session's WebSearch budget (200/200) was consumed before I could run planned queries on regional ICT/fintech trade press (Netokracija, ICTbusiness, Fintech Balkans/Serbia) and on Montenegrin business portals Portal Analitika, Ekonomist.me and Standard.co.me.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two final queries returned a budget-exhausted notice instead of results; those outlets remain unassessed for this cell.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Regional ICT trade press is the most likely place to find named core-banking, card-processing and ATM/POS vendor wins that Montenegrin general media never report, so this is a substantive rather than cosmetic gap.

negative_findings.description: Despite two dedicated queries, no vijesti.me, pobjeda.me or cdm.me article URL was returned by search — only encyclopaedic pages about the outlets and unrelated procurement portals.
negative_findings.result_summary: Flagship Montenegrin dailies are listed as low-confidence, unverified candidates rather than confirmed finds.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These are the cell's primary named targets. Their absence from results is most likely a search-index/geo-coverage artefact (US-only search) rather than evidence the sites are inactive, but it means the collection pipeline must verify them by direct fetch before relying on them.

negative_findings.description: Local-language searches combining bank + informacioni sistem + tender/nabavka returned only state procurement portals and generic bank pages; no media article about a Montenegrin commercial bank procuring an information system was found.
negative_findings.result_summary: The only confirmed bank-sector procurement story found is a central-bank one (CBCG treasury/cash-processing equipment via the EU Funding & Tenders portal), not a commercial-bank IT tender.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Supports the cell rationale that private-bank contracts are largely invisible; it also suggests media mentions of bank IT deals will more often surface as vendor press releases or signing-ceremony items than as tender reporting, which should shape query design.

negative_findings.description: Targeted query for standard.co.me and aktuelno.me returned nothing confirming these as active Montenegrin outlets covering procurement; only Antena M was confirmed as an outlet.
negative_findings.result_summary: standard.co.me and aktuelno.me are deliberately NOT listed as candidates — I did not find them, so inventing entries for them would be fabrication.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents a plausible-looking but unevidenced source from entering the registry; they should be re-tested in a later run with a live-fetch check rather than search.

negative_findings.description: No URL in this slice was fetched or otherwise confirmed reachable; all entries rest on search-result evidence or, where flagged, on prior knowledge.
negative_findings.result_summary: All URLs are supplied as unverified with per-source confidence scores.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The downstream deterministic verification pass must treat every entry as unverified; a 403 or timeout on any of these should be read as bot-defence, not death.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated 'authorised distributor / reseller' directory for POS terminal and ATM hardware brands (Ingenico, PAX, Verifone, Diebold Nixdorf, NCR/NCR Atleos, Hyosung) covering Montenegro was located via local-language search.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searching 'ovlašćeni distributer partner Crna Gora POS terminali bankomati' returned only bank-side product pages (Addiko, CKB, Erste), not vendor partner-locator pages. Global vendor partner locators were not reached in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Reseller/partner pages are one of the four channel types this cell is meant to cover; without them, the hardware-supply layer of the Montenegrin market stays invisible until an award notice appears.

negative_findings.description: The UBCG member list and the ICT Cortex / Privredna komora member directories were identified from search summaries but their exact member-list URLs were not opened in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only ubcg.info/o-nama-2-2/ and ictcortex.me/en/ were surfaced; the canonical 'članice'/'članovi' URLs remain unconfirmed. Count of 11 UBCG member banks comes from a secondary (Facebook/press) mention, not the association site.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These are the cell's core pointer sources; the URL paths must be pinned by the deterministic verification pass before they are put on a crawl schedule.

negative_findings.description: LinkedIn — likely the richest hiring-signal channel for a market this small — is login-walled and ToS-restricted for automated collection.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only public showcase/company landing URLs are visible from search; job posts and 'go-live' posts are not retrievable programmatically.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's core hypothesis (a vacancy naming a platform precedes the contract) is weakest exactly where the data is richest; budget for manual review or a licensed feed.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegro-specific IPO pipeline or capital-markets prospectus feed dedicated to banks was found beyond the SCMN/Montenegroberza filings tree.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search surfaced individual Prva banka prospectus PDFs hosted on scmn.me but no structured issuer-disclosure index or RSS.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Capex disclosure will have to be mined by crawling and PDF-parsing rather than subscribing to a feed, which raises collection cost and latency.

negative_findings.description: The session's web-search budget (200/200) was consumed before I could run planned queries for Službeni list Crne Gore (the official gazette), the Državna revizorska institucija (state audit institution) procurement audits, the European Commission's annual Montenegro enlargement report Chapter 5 section, and named regional law firms (Karanović, Prelević, Moravcevic Vojnovic, Harrisons, BDK).
negative_findings.result_summary: Those four source families are almost certainly present and relevant but are NOT documented here because I did not actually verify them in this run.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The official gazette is the only legally authoritative publication venue for amendments and bylaws, and the state audit institution is the main body reporting on non-compliant or unpublished contracts. Their absence is a real hole in this cell, not evidence they do not exist.

negative_findings.description: I found no Montenegrin law-firm publication in Montenegrin that specifically analyses the forthcoming e-invoicing obligation for public contracts. Local-language searching returned overwhelmingly Serbian material (Serbia's Zakon o elektronskom fakturisanju, paragraf.rs, KPMG Serbia), because Montenegro is licensing Serbia's platform and has no adopted law yet.
negative_findings.result_summary: Sr-language e-invoicing commentary for ME is dominated by Serbian sources; no ME-specific legal analysis surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Analysts risk mistaking Serbian obligations and deadlines for Montenegrin ones. Until a ME draft law appears, the Ministry of Finance and cross-border MoF announcements are the only reliable anchors.

negative_findings.description: The CMS Expert Guide Montenegro chapter, read in this run, describes a 'State Commission for Control of Public Procurements' and states that e-procurement and e-signatures are voluntary, and gives thresholds of EUR 25,000/30,000. This conflicts with the 2019/2023 law framework, the existing Komisija za zaštitu prava u postupcima javnih nabavki, and the operational mandatory CEJN platform.
negative_findings.result_summary: A prominent English-language legal source appears materially out of date.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: English-only research on this cell would produce wrong thresholds, a wrong remedies body name and a wrong conclusion about e-procurement being optional - a concrete demonstration of why local-language verification is mandatory.

negative_findings.description: I did not fetch cejn.gov.me, kontrola-nabavki.me or institut-alternativa.org directly in this run; they are recorded from search-result evidence and snowballing only.
negative_findings.result_summary: URLs supplied with moderate-to-high confidence but liveness and bot-defence posture are unverified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass should specifically probe CEJN, since state e-procurement portals commonly sit behind WAFs or require registration for structured data.

negative_findings.description: No annual work report of the appeals Commission (izvještaj o radu Komisije za zaštitu prava) was located at a stable URL. The Commission website menu (Aktuelnosti, Rješenja, Pravni okvir, Žalbena procedura, Stavovi/Prakse, O nama, Kontakt) shows no dedicated reports section, and caseload figures found in search results were embedded in opaque wapi.gov.me/download/<uuid> PDFs.
negative_findings.result_summary: Caseload statistics exist (e.g. 163 appeals in open procedures; 124 cases in H1 2021 including 8 arising from Administrative Court judgments) but no navigable index of these reports was found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Without a stable index, the aggregate appeals time series cannot be collected deterministically and must be reconstructed from ad-hoc PDF discovery or a direct information request.

negative_findings.description: The ujn.gov.me reports category surfaced annual procurement reports for scattered older years (2009, 2011, 2015, 2016) plus a reference to a 2022 report, rather than a clean current series.
negative_findings.result_summary: Annual national procurement reports appear split between the legacy ujn.gov.me site and the newer gov.me/mif ministry pages; no single complete index observed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Market-sizing by category requires an unbroken multi-year series; the collector must merge two hosts and may need archive.org for missing years.

negative_findings.description: The legacy portalujn.gov.me/delta2015 entry point resolves to a login page and no anonymous search path was identified. This is a hypothesis, not a verdict — a public browse route may exist on another path.
negative_findings.result_summary: Login wall observed at the only known entry URL.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Historical pre-CEJN notices and awards may be unavailable without credentials, truncating the back-series for IT/payments tenders.

negative_findings.description: The depth of anonymous public access to CEJN (cejn.gov.me) — whether notices, tender documentation and award decisions can be searched and downloaded without registration, and whether any API exists — was not established within this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Portal identified and confirmed as the statutory publication system; access mechanics unexplored.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: CEJN is the join key between appeal decisions and the underlying tender value; if it is registration-gated, the whole linkage strategy changes.

negative_findings.description: No procurement-sector index specific to banking, payments, cards or ATM/POS equipment exists in Montenegro; there is no IT/payments filter on the Commission's decision database beyond generic full-text search and CPV-style categorisation.
negative_findings.result_summary: Sector targeting must be done client-side via keyword and CPV filtering.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Every collector for this cell must implement its own sr/en keyword-and-CPV filter (softver, informacioni sistem, platni promet, kartice, bankomat, POS terminal) rather than relying on a source-side category.

negative_findings.description: The central portal cejn.gov.me/tenders could not be read by ordinary HTTP fetch: the response contained essentially only the token 'CeJN' with no tender list, filters, pagination or contracting-authority facets.
negative_findings.result_summary: Portal is live but client-rendered; content is delivered by JavaScript/XHR after page load. This is a tooling problem, not a dead source. Filter/URL semantics (whether naručilac can be filtered, whether export exists) remain UNVERIFIED.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: CeJN is the legally authoritative venue for every SOE and sector buyer in this cell. Without it, coverage rests on voluntary, often stale self-publication by the SOEs themselves. Any collection design must budget for a headless browser or reverse-engineered JSON API.

negative_findings.description: Pošta Crne Gore's javne nabavke page fetched successfully, but every notice visible on it was dated 2020 (UPS equipment, barcode readers for postal machines, monitors/keyboards, alarm-monitoring services, logistics-centre furniture).
negative_findings.result_summary: Either the page is no longer maintained (buyer migrated fully to CeJN), or newer items live on an unlinked/paginated archive not reached in this pass. Notice bodies are hosted as Google Drive links, which is fragile for long-term archiving.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Pošta is the single most payments-relevant buyer in this cell. If its own page is stale, the SOE-page strategy fails for exactly the actor the cell was created to isolate, and CeJN buyer-filtering becomes mandatory rather than a backstop.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated public-procurement URL was located for Monteput d.o.o. (roads/tolls) despite it being a payments-relevant buyer with a documented toll-equipment tender (video/ANPR system, award reported to Emovis).
negative_findings.result_summary: The tender was discoverable only via trade press (balkantraffic.com) and the company's service pages, not via a company procurement index.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Toll collection is a direct cash-handling and card-acceptance estate. If its tenders are only visible through CeJN and press, monitoring must be buyer-filtered on the central portal plus a press-keyword layer.

negative_findings.description: Čistoća d.o.o. Podgorica, a named municipal waste utility, surfaced with no independent website — only a Facebook page and a seat on the Chamber of Commerce utility association board.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language terms used ('Čistoća', 'deponija', 'komunalno preduzeće') returned Serbian rather than Montenegrin utilities for most hits; the sr-language search space here is dominated by same-named Serbian companies.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A meaningful share of the municipal-utility buyer layer likely has no self-publication surface at all, so completeness for those buyers depends entirely on CeJN and the UJN Lista naručilaca. It also flags 'Čistoća', 'Vodovod', 'Komunalno' as NOISY terms requiring a country qualifier.

negative_findings.description: Generic sr procurement terms return heavy cross-border noise. 'javne nabavke' + 'vodovod' returned Serbian utilities (Aleksinac, Požarevac, Kraljevo, Beograd); 'tenderi Crna Gora' returned scraper/spam domains (gevabiz.de) and generic global tender-resale sites (globaltenders, tendersinfo, biddetail, tendersontime).
negative_findings.result_summary: English-language querying in particular collapses into commercial tender-resale SEO farms of unverifiable provenance rather than primary sources.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Query design for this cell must pin the buyer's proper name or a .me domain filter. English-only search would have produced almost no primary sources for this cell — confirming the mandatory local-language rule.

negative_findings.description: No procurement page was located this pass for several sector buyers that certainly exist as contracting authorities: CGES (Crnogorski elektroprenosni sistem, transmission), Željeznički prevoz / Željeznička infrastruktura Crne Gore (rail), Montecargo, Barska plovidba, Regionalni vodovod Crnogorsko primorje, and the Zavod za zapošljavanje.
negative_findings.result_summary: These were identified as actors but not searched to exhaustion within this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's actor map is incomplete without them; rail and the regional water utility in particular are large, recurring buyers.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated 'Javne nabavke' or 'Plan javnih nabavki' page was found on cbcg.me. A direct fetch of the /me/javnost-rada section index returned the full subsection tree (Aktuelno, Izlaganja, Blog, Multimedija, Tenderi i oglasi, Informacije, Elektronski servisi) with no procurement-plan, contracts-register or award-notice subsection.
negative_findings.result_summary: Procurement plan is not proactively published on the CBCG website under a discoverable path; only ad-hoc 'Tenderi i oglasi' items exist.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The annual procurement plan is the single best forward-looking artefact for this cell. Its absence means the pipeline must be reconstructed from CEJN, the Strategic Plan, IFI procurement plans, and FOI requests — and yet Montenegrin media (borba.me, dan.co.me) clearly report on CBCG plan line items, so a plan document does exist and circulates somewhere.

negative_findings.description: https://cejn.gov.me/tenders returned essentially an empty shell (only the token 'CeJN') on a plain HTTP fetch, so no listing, filter model, URL pattern or registration requirement could be observed.
negative_findings.result_summary: National e-procurement portal content is not reachable without JavaScript rendering.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: CEJN is the statutory home for CBCG's domestically-run procedures. Until a headless-browser or API path is established, the entire national-portal leg of this cell is uncollectable, and CBCG award notices there would be missed.

negative_findings.description: https://www.cbcg.me/e/javnost-rada/tenderi-i-oglasi returned HTTP 404 on direct fetch even though the URL is indexed by search engines and the parallel /me/ locale path served full content.
negative_findings.result_summary: English locale of the CBCG tender page could not be retrieved on this attempt; hypothesis is locale routing or bot handling, not removal.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If the collector is pointed only at the English locale it will silently collect nothing. Collection should default to the /me/ locale with the English one as a secondary.

negative_findings.description: A targeted TED search for a Central Bank of Montenegro cash-processing notice returned only ECB tenders and unrelated Montenegro notices; the CBCG cash-equipment procurement was found instead via Montenegrin news reporting the EU Funding & Tenders Portal references EC-ENEST/TGD/2026/EA-LOP/0101 and EC-ENEST/TGD/2026/EA-LOP/0005.
negative_findings.result_summary: The notice is real and well-referenced, but it was not locatable through a generic TED keyword search.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Keyword search over TED is not a sufficient collection strategy for this cell. Collection must query the Funding & Tenders Portal by programme (EC-ENEST) and country, and must key on reference-number families, because the buyer name shown may be the Ministry of Finance rather than CBCG.

negative_findings.description: Search noise: 'Centralna banka Crne Gore' collides heavily with commercial banks carrying similar names (Prva banka Crne Gore, Prva Banka Crne Gore) and with Serbia's portal 'jnportal.ujn.gov.rs', which is a different country's system despite the near-identical acronym UJN.
negative_findings.result_summary: Several searches returned Serbian portal and commercial-bank results as top hits.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Automated collectors must pin on the exact buyer string plus a ME country/domain constraint, or they will ingest Serbian procurement and commercial-bank content as CBCG signal.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegrin-language notice was found using RTGS/RTS/X-specific procurement vocabulary ('nabavka platnog sistema', 'nadogradnja RTGS'). RTS/X coverage was found only as programme/description pages, never as a tender document.
negative_findings.result_summary: The RTS/X procurement itself (2005-generation system replaced in 2025) has no publicly discoverable notice in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single largest payment-infrastructure purchase CBCG has made in twenty years may have been procured via a route that is not publicly indexed (direct arrangement with a central-bank service provider, IFI-financed, or exempt). Establishing how RTS/X was procured is the key to predicting how the next one will be.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated IFC (private-sector arm) procurement or advisory-services notice channel specific to Montenegro financial-sector or payments projects was located during this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches surfaced only World Bank (IBRD/IDA) borrower procurement and corporate procurement pages; IFC advisory engagements in Montenegro were not visible as published tender notices.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: IFC works with commercial banks and fintechs directly and typically contracts advisers without public notices, so this channel is likely structurally opaque rather than merely unfound — collection design should not assume an IFC feed exists.

negative_findings.description: Supranational tender channels publish in English almost exclusively; local-language (sr/me) searches for donor tenders returned programme/news pages rather than notice feeds.
negative_findings.result_summary: Montenegrin-language queries on IPA digitalisation and Ministry of Finance contracting produced gov.me policy pages, EEAS news, UNDP press releases and an academic article — but the only genuinely Montenegrin-language donor-tender listing found was the ujn.gov.me 'EU tenderi' category.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: It confirms the cell's premise: this channel is an English-language island, and a Montenegrin-only monitoring strategy would miss essentially all of it. Conversely, sr-language monitoring is still needed to catch national re-publication and CFCU award information.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegro-specific EBRD procurement notice explicitly for financial-sector or payments consultancy was found in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Montenegro notices located on ECEPP were PIU support, infrastructure supervision and a wind farm; the financial-sector consultancy hypothesis remains unconfirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: EBRD's Montenegro financial-sector engagement may run through credit lines and corporate advisory (SMART by GEP) rather than client procurement, which changes which portal to monitor.

negative_findings.description: The World Bank Projects list page could not be resolved to the SEPA/TIPS project's P-number via fetch.
negative_findings.result_summary: projects.worldbank.org search page returned a near-empty JS shell; the project was instead identified through its Documents & Reports record (Report No. PADHI01235, document id 099070925154540128).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The projects portal is JS-rendered — a naive HTML crawler will silently return nothing. Collection must use the World Bank API, not page scraping. This is a rendering issue, not a dead source.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegrin commercial bank was found to operate a dedicated procurement, tender or supplier-onboarding page. NLB Banka (nlb.me), Hipotekarna banka (hipotekarnabanka.com) and Erste Bank ME (erstebank.me) were fetched directly and their navigation contains only About Us, News, Careers, Reports and Contact — no nabavka, tender, poziv za ponude, dobavljači or RFP section.
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero private-bank procurement portals in ME confirmed across three directly fetched bank sites and multiple local-language searches.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This is the defining structural fact of the cell: the primary channel the cell hypothesised (bank supplier/RFP pages) largely does not exist. Collection design must pivot to indirect routes (vendor-side press, IFI portals, exchange filings, trade press) rather than waiting on bank procurement feeds.

negative_findings.description: CKB banka (ckb.me), the largest bank in Montenegro and the most important single target of this cell, could not be fetched: both the home page and a deep 'About CKB' page returned a TLS error, 'unable to verify the first certificate'.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two fetch attempts failed on TLS chain validation, not on HTTP status.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This is almost certainly an incomplete intermediate-certificate chain served by the bank, not a dead site — the domain appears healthy in search indexes with live deep URLs. Recorded as a HYPOTHESIS of misconfiguration, not as a dead source. The collector must use a client that can complete the chain (or a headless browser) or the highest-value target in the cell will be silently missing.

negative_findings.description: No local-language evidence was found of any Montenegrin commercial bank publishing a 'poziv za dostavljanje ponuda' for IT, ATM, card, POS or core-banking goods and services. The only bank-issued public calls actually located in Montenegrin were capital-markets calls (Prva banka share and subordinated-bond issues) and a real-estate disposal call by the state-owned Razvojna banka Crne Gore.
negative_findings.result_summary: The phrase 'poziv za dostavljanje ponuda' is used by ME banks for asset disposals and securities issues, not for technology procurement.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Keyword filters built on that phrase alone will produce almost entirely false positives for A2. The filter must be a matrix of the phrase AND technology terms (bankomat, POS terminal, kartično poslovanje, core banking, softver, IT oprema), and analysts must not read a bank 'javni poziv' as a technology tender by default.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegro-specific vendor announcement was found linking a named ME bank to a named core-banking/payments supplier via a press release, despite targeted searching in both Serbian and English. The only regional core-banking contract news located concerned a Serbian bank (Asseco SEE / Privredna banka Beograd).
negative_findings.result_summary: ME-specific vendor award news is very thin in open search; the strongest ME attribution found was indirect metadata (an Asseco package id in the NLB Klik Crna Gora Google Play listing).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that for ME, technical fingerprinting (app package ids, developer names, TLS/JS assets on e-banking portals) is more productive than press monitoring, and should be built into the collection method rather than treated as a fallback.

negative_findings.description: EBRD's ECEPP portal — now the sole publication channel for EBRD-client procurement, prequalification, shortlisting and award notices — requires registration to view current notices.
negative_findings.result_summary: Registration wall confirmed by EBRD's own guidance note surfaced in search.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The most reliable mechanism that forces a private ME bank's procurement into public view sits behind a login. An account must be provisioned as a setup task, otherwise this channel yields nothing.

negative_findings.description: The cell's bank list omits Addiko Bank AD Podgorica, which EBRD reporting confirms is an operating Montenegrin bank and an active EBRD client under the Go Digital in the Western Balkans programme. UBCG is reported to have 11 member banks, more than the cell brief enumerates.
negative_findings.result_summary: At least one systemic private buyer was missing from the cell scope; the true bank count should be reconciled against the CBCG register.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A missing bank is a missing buyer. Addiko in particular is mid-digitalisation with IFI money attached, which is exactly the profile that produces visible procurement.

negative_findings.description: No public, itemised tender or award-notice feed was found for any of the four EU/Austrian/Slovenian/Hungarian parent groups (Erste, NLB, Addiko, OTP) covering supplier competitions for their Montenegrin subsidiaries. Erste and OTP expose supplier onboarding and policy documents only; Addiko exposes nothing supplier-facing at all; NLB's sole 'javni razpisi' channel publishes receivables/claims sales, not goods or services procurement.
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero parent-level public tender feeds located across Erste, NLB and Addiko; OTP exposes onboarding only. Verified by fetching the OTP supplier page, the Erste Group Procurement page and the NLB javni razpisi page directly.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale: for group-decided Montenegrin IT and payments spend there is no notice-style artefact to harvest. Collection must pivot from tender-notice scraping to onboarding-gate monitoring, press-release signal detection and disclosure-document mining.

negative_findings.description: Two of the cell's core actor acronyms are heavily polluted in English search. 'OTP ... tenders portal' returns the Ontario Tenders Portal (ontariotenders.app.jaggaer.com / ontariotenders.bravosolution.com) almost exclusively; 'NLB procurement portal' returns the Northern Lighthouse Board (nlb.delta-esourcing.com, nlb.g2b.info) and the unrelated IT firm NLB Services. English-only querying on these acronyms returns essentially zero true positives.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two English seed queries returned 100% false-positive top results; usable results only appeared after switching to hu ('beszállítói portál', 'beszerzés') and sl ('javni razpisi', 'nabava', 'dobavitelji').
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any automated crawler or alerting rule built on the bare acronyms will be swamped by Canadian and Scottish public-sector procurement noise. Queries must be entity-qualified ('OTP Bank Nyrt.', 'Nova Ljubljanska banka') or run in the parent's own language.

negative_findings.description: Targeted Montenegrin-language searches ('nabavka', 'javni poziv', 'tender', 'dobavljači') against Erste Bank AD Podgorica, NLB Banka AD Podgorica and CKB Banka surfaced no procurement, tender or supplier section on any of the three subsidiary websites.
negative_findings.result_summary: Three subsidiary sites checked via local-language search; no procurement/supplier page found on any.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Positive confirmation of the cell hypothesis — the buying signal genuinely does not appear locally — and a warning that cell 7 (local sources) will not pick these banks up either. The gap is structural, not a search failure.

negative_findings.description: No press release, award notice or vendor announcement was located tying a specific group-level card-processing, core-banking or payments framework agreement to the Montenegrin subsidiary of any of the five parents, in either English or Serbian/Montenegrin.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches on group rollout + Montenegro/CKB + card processing returned only generic corporate profile pages; no vendor-contract announcement found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Means the cell currently has no worked historical example to calibrate signal shape against. Either such announcements are made only by the vendor side (not searched exhaustively here) or they are never made public at all — which changes how confident downstream analysis may be about coverage.

negative_findings.description: https://ihale.ziraatbank.com.tr/ returned only its HTML title with no listing content. This is a hypothesis of client-side rendering or partial gating, NOT evidence the portal is dead or empty.
negative_findings.result_summary: One fetch, title only, no body content extracted.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The Ziraat portal is the most promising parent-level tender feed in this cell; writing it off on a single thin fetch would discard the best candidate. It requires a headless-browser retry before any liveness or usefulness verdict.

negative_findings.description: The cell's assigned languages are sr and en, but the decision-making parents publish procurement material in Hungarian (OTP), German (Erste), Slovenian (NLB) and Turkish (Ziraat). Serbian-language querying, though performed and mandatory, was structurally low-yield for parent-level procurement because the parents do not publish in Serbian; Serbian terms were productive only for subsidiary identity and the CBCG register.
negative_findings.result_summary: sr queries yielded actor-map and regulator sources but no parent procurement artefacts; hu/de/sl/tr queries yielded all the direct procurement sources in this slice.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A run configured strictly to sr+en will systematically under-cover this cell. Parent-language glossary coverage must be treated as in-scope for A2 even when the run's language list does not name those languages.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegrin/Serbian-language term of art was found for 'group-level framework agreement covering the subsidiary'. Local vocabulary ('okvirni sporazum', 'nabavka') is drawn from the public-procurement law lexicon and does not map onto private banking-group internal sourcing, which is conducted in English/German inside the parent.
negative_findings.result_summary: No sr-language private-sector group-sourcing terminology identified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Local-language keyword alerting cannot be relied on to catch group sourcing events; sr terms will only ever catch the downstream product launch, not the upstream decision.

negative_findings.description: Direct searches for vendor press releases announcing a signed core-banking contract with a named Montenegrin bank returned nothing specific in either language.
negative_findings.result_summary: English query 'vendor press release contract signed core banking Montenegro bank implementation' returned only generic US core-vendor negotiation content plus the Ripple–CBCG CBDC agreement; Montenegrin query with 'potpisan ugovor' + 'bankarski sistem' returned central-bank/SEPA/instant-payments items, not vendor releases.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell's premise in reverse: for a market this small, core-banking wins are largely undisclosed by both sides, so discovery must rely on indirect fingerprints (app package IDs, hosting, job ads, tender bidder lists) rather than press releases.

negative_findings.description: No Diebold Nixdorf or NCR Atleos announcement naming a Montenegrin bank was found.
negative_findings.result_summary: Query 'Diebold Nixdorf OR "NCR Atleos" Montenegro bank ATM agreement' returned only global vendor-strategy and unrelated-market items (US credit union, PayNearMe, ITCARD).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Suggests the Montenegrin ATM channel runs through regional distributors/integrators (Printec, Asseco/MoneyGet) rather than OEM-direct announcements — so distributor sources should be prioritised over OEM newsrooms.

negative_findings.description: No named digital-onboarding/eKYC vendor was found publicly attached to any Montenegrin bank.
negative_findings.result_summary: Query for Montenegro + 'digital onboarding'/'eKYC' vendor announcements returned only generic vendor marketing (Innovatrics, Microblink, Plaid) and ecosystem overviews.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A live white space: identity/onboarding suppliers to Montenegrin banks are currently unattributed in open sources and will need app-teardown, privacy-policy/processor-list and job-ad techniques.

negative_findings.description: printecgroup.com refused automated fetch.
negative_findings.result_summary: HTTP 403 Forbidden on https://www.printecgroup.com/country/printec-montenegro-en/ despite the page being indexed and summarised in search results.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A high-value supplier source for this cell needs a browser-grade collector; recording it as dead on this single failure would lose the single most relevant local vendor.

negative_findings.description: Local-language searching for card personalisation and switch/processing had weak Montenegrin terminology coverage.
negative_findings.result_summary: Queries used 'bankomati', 'POS terminali', 'ugovor', 'isporuka', 'saopštenje', 'implementacija', 'potpisan ugovor', 'reference/projekat' — but no validated Montenegrin terms were exercised for card personalisation ('personalizacija kartica'), card switching/processing ('procesiranje kartica', 'kartični switch') or kiosk ('kiosk/uređaji za samouslugu').
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Two of the cell's named solution areas (card personalisation, switch/processing) are therefore under-searched in the local language, so absence of findings for them is not evidence of absence.

negative_findings.description: The CBCG e-money institutions register was fetched directly and states that no e-money institution is currently entered.
negative_findings.result_summary: No licensed EMI in Montenegro as observed on the register page; the EMI landscape for this cell is currently empty rather than merely undocumented.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Removes an entire assumed buyer category from the current landscape and turns the register into a market-entry tripwire instead of an inventory.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Montenegrin for cash-in-transit / cash-logistics operators serving banks and ATM networks (transport gotovine, obezbjeđenje novca, agencije za zaštitu) and for any register of licensed private security agencies.
negative_findings.result_summary: No CIT operator, industry list, or Ministry of Interior licence register surfaced; results drifted to AML documents and general payment-services pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: CIT and cash-cycle operators are a named part of this coverage cell and are procurement counterparties for ATM cash management; the actor set remains unmapped.

negative_findings.description: Local-language search for a specific 2025-2026 Montenegrin bank/PSP announcement of softPOS or a Visa/Mastercard partnership returned only generic product pages, several of them Serbian and Croatian rather than Montenegrin.
negative_findings.result_summary: No datable ME-specific card-scheme or softPOS partnership announcement was located in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Partnership news is the stated primary announcement channel for this cell; failing to reach it via general search means collection must go entity-by-entity (bank/PSP newsrooms, LinkedIn) rather than by broad query.

negative_findings.description: A search for the ICT Cortex member 'POS4.me' returned no company site; results resolved instead to unrelated Montenegrin fiscalisation vendors.
negative_findings.result_summary: POS4.me exists as a cited cluster-member name but its own web presence was not confirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Illustrates that local supplier names harvested from cluster write-ups need individual domain resolution and CRPS verification before being treated as live sources.

negative_findings.description: Montenegrin-language queries about acquiring, POS terminals and card processing are heavily contaminated by Serbian, Bosnian and Croatian results because the language terms are near-identical across markets.
negative_findings.result_summary: Majority of hits for 'prihvatanje platnih kartica' and 'POS terminali' were .rs/.hr/.ba domains.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection must constrain by .me TLD or by explicit 'Crna Gora'/'Podgorica' tokens, or the corpus will be dominated by neighbouring markets and produce false attribution.

coverage_gaps.description: CeJN's internal search syntax, CPV taxonomy, notice URL pattern and pagination are unknown because the portal is JS-rendered and was not opened with a browser in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Open cejn.gov.me/tenders in a headless/real browser, capture the XHR calls behind the notice list and notice detail views, and document field names, CPV filter values and stable notice URL patterns before building the collector.

coverage_gaps.description: Simple procurements (goods/services up to EUR 15,000; works up to EUR 30,000) bypass full CeJN procedures and appear only in contracting authorities' semi-annual reports - exactly the size band of many POS terminal, terminal-maintenance and small kiosk orders.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a roster of payments-relevant contracting authorities (CBCG, Uprava prihoda i carina, Fond zdravstva, Fond PIO, Pošta CG, municipalities) and collect their polugodišnji izvještaji o jednostavnim nabavkama plus any local 'javne nabavke' pages.

coverage_gaps.description: Several likely payments-adjacent contracting authorities were reasoned about but not individually verified this pass: Fond za zdravstveno osiguranje, Fond PIO, Ministarstvo finansija/Državni trezor, Uprava za katastar, EPCG, Crnogorski elektrodistributivni sistem, Aerodromi Crne Gore, Luka Bar.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run one targeted local-language search per authority ('<naziv> javne nabavke plan nabavki') and record each own-site procurement page as a separate candidate.

coverage_gaps.description: Službeni list Crne Gore (official gazette) was not directly located or profiled, although it is the authoritative publication venue for the procurement law and its sub-regulations.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate and profile sluzbenilist.me / the official gazette portal and add it as a pointer source for procurement-law and threshold changes.

coverage_gaps.description: Coverage of award notices ('obavještenje o ishodu postupka') and signed contracts/annexes was only indirectly evidenced (a single CBCG award PDF mirrored on nabavke.com); the CeJN contract register was not located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Identify the CeJN modules for decisions, contracts and contract-execution reports and confirm whether awarded values and supplier names are exposed in a listable form; if not, use DRI audits, kontrola-nabavki.me decisions and FOI as recovery routes.

coverage_gaps.description: No confirmed English-language interface for CeJN was found; UJN offers /en/ pages but the notice content itself is Montenegrin only.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Assume sr-only notice text; budget for machine translation and build the payments keyword list natively in Montenegrin plus verbatim English technical terms.

coverage_gaps.description: The internal structure of CEJN — the URL scheme, filter parameters and any JSON/API endpoints for its plan, decision and contract modules — was not established, because the site is client-rendered and no documentation surfaced.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a browser-driven session against cejn.gov.me, capture network traffic on the plan/decision/contract searches, and document the endpoints, CPV filters and pagination. Compare against nabavke.com's /tdoc-cejn/documents/ pattern to see whether document IDs are shared.

coverage_gaps.description: No CPV code shortlist for banking and payments (ATM/POS terminals, card personalisation, cash-handling equipment, payment processing services, core banking software) was assembled for filtering Montenegrin and TED award records.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a CPV shortlist (30100000/30200000 office & data-processing equipment, 48000000 software incl. 48440000 financial-analysis, 66000000 financial services incl. 66172000 financial-transaction processing, 30162000/30144200 card-related) and use it as the primary filter on CEJN and TED, since keyword search demonstrably fails.

coverage_gaps.description: The set of Montenegrin contracting authorities that actually buy banking/payments technology was only partially identified (CBCG confirmed; Skupština, DRI, Monstat, Komunalne usluge Podgorica found as pattern examples). Uprava prihoda i carina, Ministarstvo finansija, Pošta Crne Gore, Investiciono-razvojni fond / Razvojna banka Crne Gore, Fond PIO, Fond zdravstva and the municipalities were not confirmed to have retrievable plan/contract pages.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate contracting authorities from the CEJN naručilac list, then probe each domain for /javne-nabavke/, /javne-nabavke/plan-javne-nabavke and static /userfiles/ document folders (the Monstat pattern). Prioritise CBCG, UPC, MinFin, Pošta CG and IRF.

coverage_gaps.description: No route was established for retrieving award decisions and contracts from before the current CEJN generation, nor for the pre-2019-law era under the old Uprava za javne nabavke portal.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test Wayback Machine coverage of portal.ujn.gov.me / the legacy procurement portal and of nabavke.com listing pages; check whether DRI audit reports can serve as the historical contract record for earlier years.

coverage_gaps.description: All local-language querying was done in Latin-script ijekavian Serbian. Cyrillic variants and Montenegrin-specific letters (ś, ź) were not tested, nor were transliterations of vendor names.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run key queries in Cyrillic (одлука о избору најповољније понуде, план јавних набавки, уговор) and with Montenegrin orthography, and add transliterated vendor-name variants, to check whether any register or authority publishes in Cyrillic.

coverage_gaps.description: CEJN is described as covering contract execution reports (izvještaji o izvršenju ugovora) and Institut alternativa flags contract amendments (aneksi ugovora) as under-reported, but no actual annex or execution-report artefact was located in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Specifically hunt for 'aneks ugovora' and 'izvještaj o izvršenju ugovora' artefacts inside CEJN and in DRI audit reports; these carry the real final value of a contract, which often diverges from the awarded value.

coverage_gaps.description: Whether nabavke.com's award documents and detail pages are fully open or partly subscription-gated, and what its terms of service say about automated collection, was not determined.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch nabavke.com's terms/pricing pages (e.g. /compdocs/cpp.html surfaced in search) and test whether a sample of detail pages resolves without a session before designing any crawl.

coverage_gaps.description: No confirmed public list of fiscalisation-approved POS/ENU device and software vendors was located, so the terminal supply chain remains unenumerated at the authoritative level.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch the tax authority (Uprava prihoda i carina) fiscalisation section directly and, if nothing is published, send a freedom-of-information / direct request to efiskalizacija@tax.gov.me for the register of registered software producers.

coverage_gaps.description: The roster of contracting authorities (naručioci) — public and sectoral — was not extracted; only the legal definition and the registration mechanism were confirmed. Municipalities and state-owned enterprises (Pošta CG, utilities) are likely a large share of POS-adjacent demand.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Log in / browse CEJN (cejn.gov.me) and the ujn.gov.me annual reports to extract the full naručilac list into the buyer master-table, then hand it to the notice-monitoring cells.

coverage_gaps.description: Insurance supervision (Agencija za nadzor osiguranja) and microcredit/leasing institution registers were referenced conceptually via CBCG's financial-system pages but no specific register URL was confirmed for the insurance supervisor.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch https://www.cbcg.me/me/kljucne-funkcije/finansijska-stabilnost/finansijski-sistem-crne-gore and the state-institutions link directory to resolve the insurance supervisor's current name, domain and register URLs.

coverage_gaps.description: None of the identified registers were confirmed to offer an API, bulk export or open-data dump; all appear to be HTML pages or form-driven search.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Check data.gov.me (Montenegrin open-data portal) for machine-readable copies of CRPS, procurement and state-aid data before committing to scrapers.

coverage_gaps.description: EU-level pointer assets that would list Montenegrin buyers and awards (TED, EU IPA-funded contract award databases, EBRD/World Bank procurement notice archives) were not covered in this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Assign a follow-up pass to IFI/EU procurement archives, which frequently fund Montenegrin banking-sector and fiscalisation IT projects and publish awarded-supplier names.

coverage_gaps.description: Pricing, licensing terms and redistribution rights for every commercial aggregator in this cell (eTenderi.me, TenderiLIVE, eKapija Tenderi, javne-nabavke.com, MontenegroTenders, TendersOnTime, TendersInfo, GlobalTenders, DevelopmentAid) are unknown; none were verified against their ToS.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated access review: capture each ToS/pricing page, record whether machine ingestion of alert e-mails is permitted, and rank by cost per unit of incremental recall over the free CeJN + opendata.gov.me baseline.

coverage_gaps.description: It is unknown how much each aggregator adds over the official CeJN portal, or how much the aggregators duplicate one another — especially the global family (MontenegroTenders, TendersOnTime, TendersInfo, GlobalTenders) which may all resell the same harvest.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a recall/latency benchmark: take a fixed 30-day window of ME banking/IT notices from cejn.gov.me and measure each aggregator's hit rate, publication lag, and archive retention for deleted notices.

coverage_gaps.description: Private-sector RFPs from Montenegrin commercial banks and payment institutions are largely uncovered; only eKapija claims commercial-company tenders, and that claim is unverified for ME specifically.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test eKapija's ME private-tender depth with a targeted search on bank names; if thin, plan direct monitoring of bank procurement/vendor pages as a complementary channel outside this cell.

coverage_gaps.description: Archive depth — how far back each aggregator retains notices the original publisher has deleted — was not established for any source in this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: For the two or three highest-value aggregators, query for notices older than five years and record the earliest retrievable notice date; note whether award/amendment history is retained.

coverage_gaps.description: Local-language (sr/cnr) discovery surfaced ME-focused services well, but no Albanian-language channel was checked despite a significant Albanian-speaking minority and cross-border AL/XK vendor activity.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add an Albanian-language query pass (tenderë, prokurim publik, njoftim kontrate, Mali i Zi) to test for AL/XK aggregators carrying Montenegrin notices.

coverage_gaps.description: Only one fetch was attempted in this cell and it failed at the transport layer; all other URLs come from search-result metadata and have not been retrieved.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Let the deterministic verification pass resolve HTTP status for every URL; specifically re-test etenderi.me and the http-only ekapija-tenderi.com domain, which may redirect to https or to ekapija.com.

coverage_gaps.description: Internal audit function (interna revizija) inside ministries, state funds and the central bank, and the Ministry of Finance's central harmonisation unit for internal audit, were not covered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search sr terms 'interna revizija', 'Centralna jedinica za harmonizaciju', 'godišnji izvještaj o internoj reviziji u javnom sektoru' and locate the consolidated annual internal-audit report.

coverage_gaps.description: Parliamentary oversight of audit findings (Skupština Crne Gore, Odbor za ekonomiju, finansije i budžet; Odbor za antikorupciju) not explored — search budget ran out.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Crawl skupstina.me committee pages for sessions considering DRI reports and anti-corruption hearings; capture transcripts and submitted materials.

coverage_gaps.description: No auditor/watchdog output located that names IT or payment-services suppliers to Montenegrin public banks/financial institutions, which is the commercial core of the run scope.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pivot to entity-driven collection: enumerate DRI audits of financially-relevant auditees (Ministarstvo finansija, Uprava prihoda i carina, Fond PIO, Fond zdravstvenog osiguranja, Investiciono-razvojni fond, Centralna banka) and grep those PDFs for vendor names and 'informacioni sistem' procurement line items.

coverage_gaps.description: Montenegrin-Cyrillic and alternative orthography variants (e.g. 'јавне набавке', 'ревизија') were not used as search variants; only Latin-script Montenegrin/Serbian and English were searched.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run key queries in Cyrillic transliteration and with 'ijekavica' variants ('izvještaj' vs 'izveštaj', 'sprječavanje' vs 'sprečavanje' — note ASK itself appears under both spellings).

coverage_gaps.description: No check was made for RSS feeds, sitemaps, or open-data/API endpoints on dri.co.me, institut-alternativa.org, antikorupcija.me, so collection method recommendations are crawl-based assumptions.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe /feed, /rss, /sitemap.xml and wp-json endpoints on the WordPress-based NGO sites (IA, MANS, CGO, CIN-CG all appear WordPress-based) to switch from scraping to structured feeds.

coverage_gaps.description: Transparency International's regional/national presence, the EU Commission's annual Montenegro country report (Chapter 5 – public procurement), and the EU Delegation's monitoring were not separately profiled.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add the EC enlargement country report series and TI regional procurement indices as external-oversight sources; they carry heavy weight in Montenegrin policy debate.

coverage_gaps.description: No regional ICT/fintech trade press assessed (Netokracija, ICTbusiness.info, Fintech Serbia/Balkans, Kapital.hr tech desks) — the channel most likely to name core-banking, card-processing and ATM/POS vendors winning Montenegrin bank deals.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run this cell with fresh search budget, querying vendor-side terms in local language: 'core banking implementacija banka Crna Gora', 'kartično poslovanje procesing centar', 'bankomat POS terminali nabavka'.

coverage_gaps.description: No enumeration of Montenegrin commercial banks' own newsrooms/press sections, which typically publish signing announcements and vendor partnerships that media then pick up.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate press/news pages for CKB (OTP), NLB Banka CG, Prva banka CG, Erste Bank CG, Hipotekarna banka, Lovćen banka, Adriatic Bank, Universal Capital Bank, Ziraat Bank Montenegro, and check each for a tenders/nabavke page as Crnogorski Telekom has.

coverage_gaps.description: Only Latin-script Montenegrin/Serbian terms were used. Dan publishes under a Cyrillic masthead (ДАН appeared in results), and Cyrillic-script queries were never run.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Repeat core queries in Cyrillic (јавне набавке, тендер, уговор, банка, поништен тендер) and with ijekavian variants (nabavke/nabavki, ugovoru).

coverage_gaps.description: Search surfaced mostly current-year items; no assessment of archive depth, paywall history or availability of past-year procurement affairs in any outlet.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe each confirmed outlet's archive/pagination and check Wayback coverage before choosing between live polling and retrospective backfill.

coverage_gaps.description: CIN-CG (Centar za istraživačko novinarstvo Crne Gore) was queried but search resolved to the Bosnian CIN instead; the Montenegrin investigative centre's own domain was never returned, so it is not listed as a candidate.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Resolve CIN-CG's actual domain by direct fetch/name search and add it — it is a high-value procurement-investigation publisher for this cell.

coverage_gaps.description: Several listed pointers (eKapija, Tenderi Live, javne-nabavke.com, SeeNews, Bloomberg Adria) are paywalled or subscription-gated, so unlicensed automated collection is not appropriate.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Decide licensing per source; restrict automated collection to open outlets (Bankar.me, Investitor.me, Dan, MANS) and treat gated aggregators as manual corroboration lookups.

coverage_gaps.description: Global hardware/software vendor partner-locator pages filtered to Montenegro (Ingenico, PAX, Verifone, Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, Hyosung, Temenos, Oracle FS, Finastra, BPC, OpenWay, Halcom, Comtrade, S&T/Kontron) were not enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass over each named vendor's 'partners'/'find a partner'/'contact - Montenegro' page and record the named local partner entity; then cross-check those entities against the Montenegrin company register (CRPS).

coverage_gaps.description: Non-bank PSPs, e-money institutions and payment institutions licensed by CBCG were not separately enumerated; hiring and partner signals from that segment are uncovered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Harvest the CBCG register of payment institutions/e-money institutions, then apply the same careers-page and app-metadata treatment used for banks.

coverage_gaps.description: No searching was done in Montenegrin Cyrillic script or with Albanian-language terms (used by part of the Montenegrin population and by regional integrators operating from Kosovo/Albania).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Repeat the core hiring and partner queries in Cyrillic transliteration and add Albanian terms (punë, bankë, terminale POS, partner i autorizuar) to catch missed listings.

coverage_gaps.description: Job ads and event sponsor pages are highly perishable — ads expire in weeks and sponsor logo walls are replaced each edition — yet no archival strategy is established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Register all cell URLs with a web-archive submission routine and store full-text snapshots locally on every poll, so the pre-award signal remains reconstructable after the award appears.

coverage_gaps.description: Bank annual reports published on the banks' own investor-relations pages (as opposed to CBCG/SCMN copies) were not individually located; these often carry richer narrative on digitalisation programmes.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a per-bank IR/'Izvještaji' URL list for all licensed banks and crawl annually.

coverage_gaps.description: Službeni list Crne Gore (official gazette) is not documented as a monitored source, despite being the only legally definitive publication venue for the Law on Public Procurement, its amendments and every bylaw.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: In the next run, locate and register the official gazette's search interface and its procurement-related issue feed; anchor all amendment detection to gazette issue numbers (e.g. 074/19, 003/23, 011/23).

coverage_gaps.description: No state audit institution (Državna revizorska institucija) or budget-inspection source captured. Montenegro's Chapter 5 commitments explicitly include strengthened budget-inspection controls, so audit reports will be the main evidence of contracts awarded outside published procedures.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Register the DRI report archive and the Ministry of Finance budget-inspection outputs; filter audits for IT/payments spending.

coverage_gaps.description: The European Commission's own Montenegro enlargement/progress report and the EU Council common position on Chapter 5 were referenced only second-hand through eu.me and national press; the primary EU documents are not registered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add the EC enlargement package Montenegro country report and the Chapter 5 negotiating/common position documents as tracked primary sources.

coverage_gaps.description: Reporting flagged a March 2025 Montenegro-UAE intergovernmental cooperation agreement that exempts certain contracts from procurement procedures. Contracts under such bilateral instruments never reach CEJN and are invisible to every notice-scanning cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a standing tracker of international agreements, defence/security exemptions and PPP/concession routes that legally bypass the procurement portal.

coverage_gaps.description: Only one domestic Montenegrin law firm was identified with a procurement angle, and no regional firm (Karanović, BDK, Harrisons, Moravcevic Vojnovic, Prelević) was verified as publishing ME procurement commentary.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Crawl the Advokatska komora Crne Gore member directory and the Podgorica offices of regional firms for 'javne nabavke' practice pages and publication feeds.

coverage_gaps.description: The Q2 2026 commitments (amended Law on Public Procurement, amended anti-corruption law, red-flag module in the e-procurement system) have no single tracked document trail; they are currently known only through news and eu.me summaries.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate the government action plan / Chapter 5 roadmap document that enumerates these commitments and track it as the canonical reform pipeline artefact.

coverage_gaps.description: The Commission decision database's underlying query mechanics (URL parameters, pagination, whether decision PDFs are directly addressable) were not reverse-engineered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a browser-driven pass over kontrola-nabavki.me/rjesenja to capture the search request, response shape and PDF URL pattern; document a stable enumeration recipe.

coverage_gaps.description: Parliamentary oversight of procurement bodies (Skupština Crne Gore — Odbor za ekonomiju, finansije i budžet, and Odbor za antikorupciju) was not directly searched; committee hearings and adopted reports on the Commission and DRI are a likely source of aggregate data and political signals.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search skupstina.me for 'izvještaj o radu' of the Commission and DRI, and for committee sessions on javne nabavke.

coverage_gaps.description: Agencija za sprječavanje korupcije (ASK) and Uprava za inspekcijske poslove were not covered; ASK handles conflict-of-interest and integrity plans in procurement, and inspection bodies conduct procurement-compliance supervision.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Dedicated search pass on antikorupcija.me and uip.gov.me for procurement-related supervision reports.

coverage_gaps.description: Službeni list Crne Gore (official gazette) was not indexed as a source for procurement-law amendments and bylaws establishing thresholds and appeal fees.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add sluzbenilist.me as a legal-baseline source with keyword monitoring on 'javne nabavke'.

coverage_gaps.description: Coverage relied on Montenegrin/Serbian latinica.
